title: 406. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Coterminal Angles and Reference Angles
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an angle coterminal with a given angle by adding a full turn.
questions.question: Which angle is coterminal with \(50^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Coterminal angles differ by a multiple of \(360^\circ\). Since \(410^\circ-50^\circ=360^\circ\), the angles \(410^\circ\) and \(50^\circ\) share a terminal side. In contrast, \(230^\circ-50^\circ=180^\circ\), which is only a half turn.
questions.hint: Subtract the two angles and check whether the difference is a whole number of full turns.

questions.concept: Least positive coterminal angle of a negative angle
questions.learningObjective: Find the least positive angle coterminal with a negative angle.
questions.question: What is the least positive angle coterminal with \(-60^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Add one full turn: \(-60^\circ+360^\circ=300^\circ\). This is positive, and subtracting \(360^\circ\) again would make it negative, so it is the least positive coterminal angle. The angle \(60^\circ\) is the reflection of \(-60^\circ\) in the \(x\)-axis, not a coterminal angle.
questions.hint: Add \(360^\circ\) repeatedly until the result is positive for the first time.

questions.learningObjective: Find the reference angle of an angle whose terminal side is in Quadrant II.
questions.question: What is the reference angle of \(150^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle is the acute angle between the terminal side and the \(x\)-axis. For an angle in Quadrant II it is \(180^\circ-150^\circ=30^\circ\). The value \(60^\circ=150^\circ-90^\circ\) measures the angle from the \(y\)-axis, which is not the reference angle.
questions.hint: Measure the acute angle from the terminal side to the nearest part of the \(x\)-axis.

questions.learningObjective: Find the reference angle of an angle whose terminal side is in Quadrant III.
questions.question: What is the reference angle of \(250^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The terminal side of \(250^\circ\) lies in Quadrant III, between \(180^\circ\) and \(270^\circ\). The reference angle is measured from the \(x\)-axis: \(250^\circ-180^\circ=70^\circ\). The value \(20^\circ=270^\circ-250^\circ\) is measured from the \(y\)-axis instead.
questions.hint: In Quadrant III, subtract \(180^\circ\) from the angle.

questions.learningObjective: Find the reference angle of a Quadrant IV angle given in radians.
questions.question: What is the reference angle of \(\frac{5\pi}{3}\)?
questions.explanation: The angle \(\frac{5\pi}{3}\) lies between \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) and \(2\pi\), so it is in Quadrant IV. The reference angle is \(2\pi-\frac{5\pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{3}\). The value \(\frac{2\pi}{3}=\frac{5\pi}{3}-\pi\) is not acute, so it cannot be a reference angle.
questions.hint: In Quadrant IV, subtract the angle from a full turn; a reference angle is always acute.

questions.learningObjective: Find the least positive angle coterminal with an angle larger than two full turns.
questions.question: What is the least positive angle coterminal with \(1000^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract full turns: \(1000^\circ-2\cdot 360^\circ=1000^\circ-720^\circ=280^\circ\), which lies between \(0^\circ\) and \(360^\circ\). The value \(80^\circ=360^\circ-280^\circ\) is the reference angle of \(280^\circ\), not a coterminal angle.
questions.hint: Subtract as many multiples of \(360^\circ\) as possible while keeping the result positive.

questions.concept: Reference angle of a negative angle
questions.learningObjective: Find the reference angle of a negative angle by first finding a coterminal angle.
questions.question: What is the reference angle of \(-200^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: First find a coterminal angle: \(-200^\circ+360^\circ=160^\circ\), which is in Quadrant II. Its reference angle is \(180^\circ-160^\circ=20^\circ\). The value \(160^\circ\) is the coterminal angle itself; it is not acute, so it is not the reference angle.
questions.hint: Replace the angle by its least positive coterminal angle, then find the acute angle to the \(x\)-axis.

questions.learningObjective: Decide which radian measure is coterminal with a given radian measure.
questions.question: Which angle is coterminal with \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\)?
questions.explanation: Coterminal angles differ by a multiple of \(2\pi\). Here \(\frac{5\pi}{6}-\left(-\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{12\pi}{6}=2\pi\), so \(-\frac{7\pi}{6}\) is coterminal with \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\). However, \(\frac{7\pi}{6}-\frac{5\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{3}\), which is not a multiple of \(2\pi\).
questions.hint: Subtract each candidate from \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) and check whether the difference is a multiple of \(2\pi\).

questions.learningObjective: Write a formula for every angle coterminal with a given angle.
questions.question: Which expression describes all angles coterminal with \(40^\circ\), where \(k\) is any integer?
questions.explanation: Two angles in standard position share a terminal side exactly when they differ by a whole number of full turns, so the family is \(40^\circ+360^\circ k\). The expression \(40^\circ+180^\circ k\) also includes \(220^\circ\) (for \(k=1\)), whose terminal side points in the opposite direction.
questions.hint: Test each formula with \(k=1\) and check whether the result has the same terminal side as \(40^\circ\).

questions.concept: Reference angle of a large negative radian measure
questions.learningObjective: Combine coterminal reduction and reference angles for a radian measure.
questions.question: What is the reference angle of \(-\frac{17\pi}{6}\)?
questions.explanation: Add two full turns: \(-\frac{17\pi}{6}+4\pi=-\frac{17\pi}{6}+\frac{24\pi}{6}=\frac{7\pi}{6}\). This coterminal angle is in Quadrant III, so the reference angle is \(\frac{7\pi}{6}-\pi=\frac{\pi}{6}\). The value \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) is not acute, so it cannot be a reference angle.
questions.hint: Add multiples of \(2\pi\) until the angle is between \(0\) and \(2\pi\), then measure to the \(x\)-axis.
